title: Hydrogen storage in bulk graphene-related materials
material_description: 2300m²/g | KOH-activated reduced graphene oxide (thermally exfoliated Hummers graphite oxide activated with KOH); assigned to the KOH-activated group from its surface area (paper: exfoliation alone gave at most ~850 m²/g, activation gave 1000-2300 m²/g; Figs 2 and 5 label this region "rHGO activated by KOH")
activation_method: KOH activation of the thermally exfoliated graphite oxide (grinding with KOH and annealing in Ar at 800 °C, or impregnation with KOH solution); which procedure was used for this sample is not stated
source_location: main-02.png (paper p. 1), Abstract; pressure from Figure 5 caption, main-18.png (paper p. 17)
notes: Printed: "Linear increase of hydrogen adsorption vs surface area was observed at 77 K with maximal observed value of ~5 Wt% for 2300 m2/g sample." No pressure is printed with the value; 50 bar is taken from the Figure 5 caption ("Hydrogen uptakes measured by volumetric method at ambient (120 Bar) and 77K (50 Bar)"), the figure that plots these 77 K maximal uptakes against BET area. Figure 4 shows this sample's 77 K isotherm (I1), whose highest-pressure marker is at 38.75 bar, 5.0975 wt% (archive: fig4_2300.json); the value is within 3% of it, but it is not merged because its stated pressure (50 bar) is not within 2% of any plotted point and the paper does not say it was taken from Figure 4, so it carries no isotherm_id. Volumetric, Hiden Isochema Intelligent Manometric Instrument (IMI), liquid-nitrogen immersion cell at 77 K; free-volume determination not described; no uncertainty reported. Degassing and sample mass for the 77 K runs not stated. BET area is the curve label in Figure 4 (and the abstract: "2300 m²/g sample") (N2 adsorption, Quantachrome Nova 1200e); the paper says some samples lost 10-15% of their area during H2 runs and Fig. 2 uses the final value, but does not say whether this label is the value before or after the H2 measurement.

title: Hydrogen storage in bulk graphene-related materials
material_description: 1740 m²/g | KOH-activated reduced graphene oxide (thermally exfoliated Hummers graphite oxide activated with KOH); assigned to the KOH-activated group from its surface area (paper: exfoliation alone gave at most ~850 m²/g, activation gave 1000-2300 m²/g; Figs 2 and 5 label this region "rHGO activated by KOH")
activation_method: KOH activation of the thermally exfoliated graphite oxide (grinding with KOH and annealing in Ar at 800 °C, or impregnation with KOH solution); which procedure was used for this sample is not stated
source_location: main-17.png (paper p. 16), Figure 3 (293 K), series 1740 m²/g (black squares), highest-pressure marker at pixel (832.0, 284.5)
notes: archive: fig3_1740.json Only the highest-pressure point is extracted (isotherm not at 77 K). Gravimetric (Rubotherm system; model not named). Paper: FLUIDCAL used to calculate fluid density of H2 and He, but a buoyancy correction is not stated explicitly, so basis_inferred = unknown and calibration_described = false. Uncertainty: "precision in measured uptake values is estimated to be ± 0.02 Wt% for typical 200 mg sample". Degassing not stated per sample (paper: usually 150-300 °C under high vacuum for 12-16 h; most Fig. 2 samples at 150 °C); sample mass not stated per sample (typical 100-300 mg). BET area is the curve label in Figure 3 (N2 adsorption, Quantachrome Nova 1200e); the paper says some samples lost 10-15% of their area during H2 runs and Fig. 2 uses the final value, but does not say whether this label is the value before or after the H2 measurement. Black markers of all Fig. 3 curves were digitized in one run (fig3_black_combined_run.json) and assigned to curves. 5 markers counted for this curve; one further marker at the origin is shared by all curves and not attributed.
